supported_new_design_changes: Introduce a calibration-only empirical release-versus-retain branch instead of only changing final delta scoring.
Audit evidence, release decisions and independent test gains under prespecified adaptation and control-reference conventions.
Separate within-dataset context/perturbation/joint holdouts from zero-shot cross-dataset transfer and from combinatorial prediction.
Pin original source commits and treat configuration declarations as inputs to a later actual-split audit.
corrections: PCA-linear remains a feasible prediction baseline under appropriate training inputs; it must not be grouped with held-out-response duplicate controls as evaluation-only.
Library accepted-version labels do not independently establish journal acceptance or peer review; this review makes no such claim.
Two control-mean arrays or disjoint cell halves do not establish biological independence; experiment-level sampling and assignment must establish that condition.

predict(fold) returns the selected reference-fold prediction under a common release decision, falling back to the pooled source if rejected; it does not emit two independently chosen candidate models simultaneously.
Near-universal release alone does not prove lack of discrimination; inspect independent gains, risks and uncertainty instead.
SafeDelta release also requires finite evidence; nonfinite or nonpositive evidence is rejected.
The unread pcc/core.py implementation belongs to SafeDelta, not PIE; its earlier local-agent reading is not counted as this DeepSeek run.
This completed source-query checkpoint neither establishes that historical citation expansion never occurred nor that its historical graph is current.
reviewer_reading_boundary: The independent reviewer previously read SafeDelta core.py in a separate local-agent session. None of those 7661 characters or reads are included in the current DeepSeek totals; current scientific claims are checked against the four observed source documents and clearly stated design judgment.
